14th October, 2024.

R e s p o n d e n t s _________________________________________________________________ Coram Ms. Justice Jyotsna Rewal Dua, lWhether approved for reporting?
__ __ For the petitioners: Mr. Vinod Chauhan, Advocate.
For the respondents: Ms. Leena Guleria, Deputy Advocate General.
Jyotsna Rewal Dua, Judge
With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, matter is heard at this stage.

2. Case set up by the petitioners is that they are co- owners in possession of the land comprised in Khata No.61 min/57, Khatauni No. 161 min/161,
Khasra No.627, situated in Mohal Bella, Patwar Circle Bandli, Tehsil Shillai, District Sirmour, H.P.
Jamabandi for the year 2018-19, evidencing this has been placed on record.
According to the petitioners, respondents l
Whether reporters of Local Papers may be allowed to see the judgment?
yes constructed Bella-Siyasu road via Dimti and Parli Farad.
In construction of this road, aforesaid land of the petitioners was utilized.
However, the petitioners have not been paid any compensation in lieu of use of their land for the construction of the road.
The land of the petitioners utilized in construction of the road, has not been acquired in accordance with law.

With this grievance, this writ petition has been filed, seeking direction to the respondents to start acquisition process for acquiring the subject land and awarding suitable compensation to the petitioners.
3. The respondents in their reply have not denied utilizing the land of the petitioners for the construction of Bella-Siyasu road under H.P. Public Works Department Shillai Division.

entities.text: H.P. Public Works Department Shillai Division
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
According to the respondents, the construction of the road was carried out on persistent demand of the people of the area including the petitioners for providing them road connectivity during the year 2006-07,
which was completed in the year 2010.
The respondents' case is that the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners alongwith other villagers had voluntarily offered their land for construction of the road.

They had never raised any objection or demand for compensation of the land since the _________________________________________________________________ vs State Of H.P. & Ors on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183238653/
1 construction of the road till the date of the filing of the petition.

Hence, pleas of delay and laches as also voluntary surrendering of the land by the petitioners have been taken for opposing petitioners'
prayer.

It had also been submitted that the road had been constructed under the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana and the road under the said scheme can be constructed only when the landowners provide land free of cost.
There is no provision for granting any compensation for the land utilized for construction of road under the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana.
4. At this state, learned counsel for the petitioners placed on record a judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Division Bench of this Court in Nathu Ram & another Vs. State of H.P. & other1.

entities.text: Nathu Ram & another Vs. State of H.P. & other1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the petitioners contended that the case of the petitioners is squarely covered in terms of the aforesaid judgment, which was rendered in a case where the land of the petitioners, therein,
situated at same Patwar Circle Bandli, Tehsil Shillai, District Sirmour, H.P. was utilized for construction of Bella-Siyasu road under HPPWD Shillai Division.

The respondents, therein, had taken CWP No. 3452 of 2023 decided on 19.07.2023 the same ground as taken herein for opposing the prayers made in the aforesaid case for acquiring the utilized land in accordance with law by paying compensation in accordance with law.

In the aforesaid case, on considering the entire case record and pleadings of the parties, the Hon'ble Division Bench had allowed the writ petition and directed the respondents to demarcate the land of the petitioners (therein) utilized for construction of the road in question within four weeks, by taking it as having been acquired for the said purpose in the year 2010 and then to pay compensation to the petitioners under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 with all statutory benefits.

Relevant paras of the judgment run as under:-
In this Writ petition, the petitioners contend that they are absolute owners of land comprised in Khata- Khatauni no. 75/202, Khasra no. 629, 575 etc., situated at Mohal Bella, Patwar Circle Bandli, Tehsil Shillai, District Sirmour, Himachal Pradesh which was inherited by them from their father late Sh. Guman Singh and which is of extent two bighas.
They have filed Annexure-P-1- Jamabandi for the year 2018-19 which supports their claim.
2. They allege that without acquiring any portion of their land, the respondents have laid a link road from Bella to Siyasu under HP PWD Shillai recently.

According to them, a total extent of land owned by them is 24.13 bighas; there are many fruit plants and trees of valuable timber wood; and that while laying the road, their land was used; and it was destroyed completely and made uncultivable.

7. The defence of the respondents is that the work of construction of the said link road was started on the persistent demand of the people of the area including the petitioners to provide road connectivity during the year 2006-2007 and it was completed in the year 2010 under PMGSY Phase-1 Scheme Package No. HP- 10- 66.

It is contended that as per guidelines of the said Scheme, roads can be constructed under the Scheme only where land owners provide land free of cost and there is no provision for payment of _________________________________________________________________ vs State Of H.P. & Ors on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183238653/
2 compensation for land utilized for construction of the road.
8.
It is contended that father of the petitioners alongwith other villagers voluntarily offered their land for construction of the road and on the basis of their verbal consent, the road was laid.
9. It is contended that the writ petition was filed after 17 years from the date of construction of the road and is not maintainable.

10. Reliance is placed on a judgment of the Full Bench of this Court in CWP no. 1966/2010-C,
Shankar Dass vs. State of H.P. and it is contended that in the said Full Bench decision, the parties were directed to approach the Civil Court and so the Writ Petition should be dismissed.
11.

entities.text: Shankar Dass vs. State of H.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is contended that the demand for compensation made by the petitioners is unjustified because there was a policy decision taken by the Government of Himachal Pradesh in 1998-99 that all rural link roads would be constructed only after the land owners donate their land for construction of the road in view of limited financial resources of the State Government.
12. Other allegations about damage to the land have been denied.
19. In Sukh Dutt Ratra (6 Supra), the appellants' land had been utilized for construction of road in 1972-73 without initiating any proceedings for acquisition and without paying any compensation.

When the petitioner filed a writ petition on the basis of relief granted to other owners whose land was so acquired, the said Writ petition was dismissed by the High Court holding that there were disputed questions of law and fact for determination on the starting point of limitation, which cannot be adjudicated in the writ proceeding and the petitioners were given liberty to approach the Civil Court.

The Supreme Court reversed the said decision and held that nobody can be deprived of liberty or property without due process, or authorization of law and the State has a higher responsibility in demonstrating that it has acted within the confines of legality, and had not tarnished the basic principle of the rule of law.
It held that the State, merely on the ground of delay and laches, cannot evade its legal responsibility towards those from whom private property has been expropriated.
It observed that the State was initiating acquisition proceedings selectively and not in every case like that of the appellants whose land was taken, and at every stage it sought to shirk its responsibility of acquiring land required for public use in the manner prescribed by law.
It held that the State cannot shield itself behind the ground of delay and laches in such a situation as there cannot be a limitation to doing justice.
_________________________________________________________________ vs State Of H.P. & Ors on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183238653/
3

It also rejected the plea of alleged verbal consent or lack of objection on the ground that no material was placed on record to substantiate the said plea, and held that the State was unable to produce any evidence indicating that the land of the appellant had been taken over or acquired in the manner known to law, or that it had ever paid any compensation.
It declared that there is no period of limitation prescribed for the courts to exercise their Constitutional jurisdiction to do substantial justice.
It directed the State to treat the subject land as a deemed acquisition and disburse compensation to the appellants therein in terms of similar orders passed in other cases within four months.

20. In view of the above settled legal position, we are of the opinion that the stand of the State that it need not pay any compensation for utilizing the petitioners' land for the purpose of laying a road cannot be countenanced and the State is bound to pay market value compensation to the petitioner for utilizing his land for the purpose of the road.
21.

Accordingly, the Writ petition is allowed with costs of Rs. 10,000/- and a direction is issued to the respondents to demarcate the land of the petitioners utilized for the purpose of the road in question within four weeks, treat it as having been acquired for the said purpose in 2010 and pay to the petitioners compensation under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 with all statutory benefits there under within four months."
During course of the hearing

, learned Deputy Advocate General was directed to have instruction as to whether the case of the petitioners was similarly situated as the case of the petitioners in Nathu Ram and Another Vs. State of H.P. and Others.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned Deputy Advocate General on the basis of instructions, now submits that the case of the petitioners is similarly situated as the case of Nathu Ram and Another Vs. State of H.P. and Others and is covered by the decision rendered therein.

entities.text: Nathu Ram and Another Vs. State of H.P. and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. In view of the aforesaid submissions, this writ petition is disposed of in terms of directions issued in the case of Nathu Ram and Another Vs. State of H.P. and Others.

The writ petition is disposed of in terms of the directions issued in Nathu Ram and Another Vs. State of H.P. and Others, except the costs imposed therein.
